page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs provisioned across 4 physical Intel Xeon processor cores running at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration provides 45 MB of L3 cache alongside standard x86 extension support, including AVX, AES, FMA, and BMI2 instructions. System memory is constrained to 7.0 GB (0.9 GB per vCPU thread), resulting in a high CPU-to-memory ratio. This instance includes no bundled local NVMe storage and contains zero GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the n1-highcpu-8 displays moderate compute and memory throughput capabilities relative to broader cloud hardware baselines. Its PassMark CPU overall score reaches 6786.78, placing it in the middle tier of general compute performance, alongside an average score in Geekbench ray tracing tests (6021.0). Large block uncached memory bandwidth demonstrates solid transfer rates of 47.28 GB/sec for reads and 34.7 GB/sec for writes. However, single-core processing capabilities are comparatively low, with Geekbench single-core performance scoring 914.0 and stress-ng single-core achieving 1109.79. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression yield poor throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the n1-highcpu-8 lies in its limited memory capacity relative to its 8 virtual cores. With less than 1 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory-intensive processes or concurrent thread allocations requiring large memory footprints may experience bottlenecks. Qualitatively, this profile offers resource density tailored for compute-focused applications where low memory overhead is required, minimizing paid RAM allocations that would otherwise sit idle. Recommended workload fits include compute-centric batch processing, parallel integer workloads, lightweight CI/CD build workers, static web serving, and small-scale LLM text generation tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 Intel Xeon processors running at 2.3 GHz. Configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 7.0 GB of RAM, it offers a high CPU-to-memory ratio of 0.9 GB per thread. The processor features 45 MB of L3 cache with hardware support for AVX, AES, FMA, and BMI2 instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations show middle-tier performance in multi-core metrics, including a PassMark CPU score of 6786.78 and large block uncached memory read bandwidth of 47.28 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core processing scores and memory capacity remain modest. Lacking local SSD storage and GPU acceleration, the n1-highcpu-8 delivers a dense vCPU profile suited for compute-focused workloads with minimal RAM footprint requirements, such as lightweight CI/CD builds, parallel batch processing, static web serving, and small-scale text generation.
